text: GD's Aerospace segment, made up of Gulfstream and Jet Aviation, produces business jets and provides aircraft repair, customer support and custom completion services.
quote: Our Aerospace segment is recognized as a leading producer of business jets and the standard bearer in new technology aircraft, aircraft repair, customer support and custom completion services. The segment consists of our Gulfstream and Jet Aviation business units.

text: GD's Combat Systems segment makes and integrates land combat solutions worldwide, including wheeled and tracked combat vehicles, weapon systems, energetics and munitions.
quote: Our Combat Systems segment is a premier manufacturer and integrator of land combat solutions worldwide, including wheeled and tracked combat vehicles, weapon systems, energetics and munitions.

text: GD's Marine Systems segment designs and builds nuclear-powered submarines, surface combatants and auxiliary ships for the U.S. Navy.
quote: Our Marine Systems segment is the leading designer and builder of nuclear-powered submarines and a leader in surface combatant and auxiliary ship design and construction for the U.S. Navy.

text: GD's Technologies segment, made up of GDIT and Mission Systems, provides services, technologies and products to military, intelligence, federal civilian and state customers.
quote: Our Technologies segment provides a full spectrum of services, technologies and products to a wide range of military, intelligence, federal civilian and state customers. The segment is organized into two business units — Information Technology (GDIT) and Mission Systems

text: For the quarter, GD's book-to-bill ratio, orders divided by revenue, was 1.5-to-1 for Aerospace, 1.4-to-1 for the defense segments and 1.4-to-1 company-wide.
quote: Book-to-bill ratio, defined as orders divided by revenue, was 1.4-to-1 for the quarter for the defense segments, 1.5-to-1 for the Aerospace segment, and 1.4-to-1 on a company-wide basis.

text: GD still expects Gulfstream to deliver about 160 airplanes in 2026.
quote: For 2026, we now expect Aerospace revenue of around $13.8 billion. Gulfstream will still deliver about 160 airplanes.

text: GD anticipates a 14.7% Aerospace operating margin for the year.
quote: Gulfstream will still deliver about 160 airplanes. There is some potential upside delivering large-cabin aircraft and some risk on the 280 deliveries for obvious reasons. We anticipate a 14.7% operating margin for the year.

text: GD expects Aerospace revenue of around $13.8 billion for 2026.
quote: For 2026, we now expect Aerospace revenue of around $13.8 billion.

text: On its 2026-07-29 call GD said the final G280 ought to deliver in the second quarter of 2027 and put the onset of the G300 somewhere around late 2027 or early 2028, leaving a planned production break.
quote: the final 280 ought to deliver in the second quarter of next year, and the onset of the 300, which late '27, early '28, somewhere in that. And so we'll have a planned production break

text: Gulfstream's G280 certification release called the G280 a joint effort between Gulfstream and Israel Aerospace Industries (IAI).
quote: The G280, a joint effort between Gulfstream and Israel Aerospace Industries (IAI), offers the most comfortable cabin and the longest range at the fastest speed in its class.

text: Gulfstream builds all its large-cabin models in Savannah, Georgia, while a non-U.S. partner assembles the mid-cabin G280.
quote: Gulfstream designs, develops and manufactures aircraft in Savannah, Georgia, including all large-cabin models. The mid-cabin G280 is assembled by a non-U.S. partner.

text: GD announced its all-new super-midsize G300 in September 2025 to replace the G280.
quote: In September 2025, we announced our all-new super-midsize G300 aircraft, which will replace the G280 aircraft.

text: On its 2026-07-29 call, GD said it had stepped up its work on the G400 and would say more over the following couple of quarters about where the G400 will be.
quote: On the 400, we've whipped up our efforts on the 400, and we'll have more to say over the next couple of quarters about where we think the 400 will be

text: The G500 entered service in 2018 and the G600 in 2019.
quote: The G500 and G600 entered service in 2018 and 2019, respectively.

text: G650 production ended in the first quarter of 2025, and the G800 replaces it.
quote: The G800 is the replacement aircraft for the G650, which correspondingly ended production in the first quarter of 2025.

text: Gulfstream began G700 deliveries in the second quarter of 2024, after FAA and EASA certification.
quote: including our ultra-long-range, ultra-large-cabin G700 aircraft, which began deliveries in the second quarter of 2024 following U.S. Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) and European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) certification.

text: The FAA and EASA type certified the G800 on 2025-04-16.
quote: On April 16, 2025, the world's longest-range business aircraft, our ultra-long-range, ultra-large-cabin G800 received type certification from the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) and the European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA).

text: G800 deliveries began in the third quarter of 2025.
quote: Gulfstream aircraft deliveries, which included the G800 that began deliveries in the third quarter of 2025.

text: GD says that if Aerospace customers default on existing contracts and the contracts are not replaced, the segment's anticipated revenue and profitability could be reduced materially.
quote: In addition, if customers default on existing contracts and the contracts are not replaced, the segment’s anticipated revenue and profitability could be reduced materially.

text: GD says customer demand for its business aircraft can be affected by changes in general economic conditions, the availability and cost of credit, pricing pressures and trends in capital goods markets.
quote: Customer demand can be affected by a number of factors, including changes in general economic conditions, the availability and cost of credit, pricing pressures and trends in capital goods markets.

text: GD says it typically assumes more risk with fixed-price contracts, which offer additional profits when it completes the work for less than originally estimated.
quote: Typically, we assume more risk with fixed-price contracts. However, these types of contracts offer additional profits when we complete the work for less than originally estimated.

text: GD says non-U.S. transactions can involve increased risks from foreign exchange rate variability, which could hurt sales and the translation of international revenue into U.S. dollars, and from differing legal systems.
quote: Non-U.S. transactions can involve increased risks arising from foreign exchange rate variability, which could, among other things, negatively impact sales and the translation of our international revenue from local currencies into U.S. dollars, and differing legal systems.

text: GD says many of its new products must meet extensive, time-consuming regulatory requirements that are often outside its control and may cause unanticipated delays.
quote: Many of our new products must meet extensive and time-consuming regulatory requirements that are often outside our control and may result in unanticipated delays.

text: GD says it sometimes relies on only one or two sources of supply, and any supply chain disruption could hurt its ability to meet customer commitments.
quote: We sometimes rely on only one or two sources of supply, and any disruption in our supply chain could have an adverse effect on our ability to meet our customer commitments

text: In its 2025 annual report, GD said tariffs had not had a material impact on its results but reduced Aerospace operating margins by 30 basis points in 2025.
quote: To date, the tariffs have not had a material impact on our results but did reduce the Aerospace operating margins by 30 basis points in 2025. The duration and extent of the tariffs continue to evolve.

text: In its 2026Q2 quarterly report, GD said the U.S. Supreme Court held in February 2026 that the tariffs imposed under IEEPA were unauthorized, and that tariffs as applied and tariffs yet to be refunded are not material to its results.
quote: Overall, tariffs as applied in their current form and tariffs yet to be refunded are not material to our results of operations.

text: GD says decreases in U.S. government defense and other spending, or changes in spending allocation or priorities, could reduce, delay or terminate its programs and impact its financial performance.
quote: Decreases in U.S. government defense and other spending or changes in spending allocation or priorities could result in one or more of our programs being reduced, delayed or terminated, which could impact our financial performance.
